meta.title: Climate risk in private markets: the data gap, and what AI can and can't fix
meta.description: Private markets hold about US$17tn, and up to 90% of their emissions data is estimated. What the evidence says about climate risk in private portfolios, how AI estimates work, how wrong they can be, and a five-step plan for GPs and LPs.
faq: Can AI estimate the emissions of a private company?

Yes, but mostly from its revenue, size and sector. Studies show machine-learning models beat simple sector averages by up to about 30% on Scope 1 and 2 error, and much less on Scope 3. No published study has tested these models on private companies, so treat the output as an estimate, label it, and score it PCAF data quality 4 or 5.
How much private-markets emissions data is estimated today?
ILPA members report that as much as 90% of the emissions data they receive for private funds has to be estimated rather than reported by the company.

Yes. The EU's SFDR lets managers use reasonable assumptions where data is missing, and no regulator we found bans estimates. What regulators penalise is presenting an estimate as measured, or overstating what an AI model does.
What should a GP do first?

Collect Scope 1 and 2 on the EDCI template, calculate with the iCI standard, put a PCAF data-quality score on every figure, set a date by which each estimate becomes a measured number, and use asset-level geospatial analysis for real assets.
Which rule forces private companies to measure emissions?
California's SB 253. US companies, public or private, with more than US$1bn revenue that do business in California must file Scope 1 and 2 emissions, with the first reports due 10 November 2026.
